lines.trans: Why did you even decide to scare me?
I started panicking because of that.
You could have simply asked me to stay.
You are my closest friend after all!
What would I do without you?
Forgive me, but I am staying to work here.
Gulya, will you not object right now?
If I work here as sous-chef a bit longer?
Darling, I will support any decision of yours.
Well, then let us go quickly to the kitchen!
Otherwise we are running late for work!
Let us go, Viktor Petrovich, it is time to cook dinner.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'why', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.en: to begin, to start, to break out (intransitive)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'began, started', paired with 'начинаться'.

examples.text: Там начался пожар!
examples.trans: A fire started there!

examples.text: Фильм начался ровно в семь.
examples.trans: The film started at seven sharp.

examples.text: Там начался пожар! Везде пожарные машины и полиция!
examples.trans: A fire started there! Fire engines and police are everywhere!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'panic' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня от этого началась паника.
examples.trans: I started panicking because of that.

examples.text: На корабле началась паника.
examples.trans: Panic began on the ship.

examples.text: Среди испуганных пассажиров началась ужасная паника.
examples.trans: Among frightened passengers a terrible panic began.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сейчас всё выглядит очень некрасиво.
examples.trans: Right now everything looks very bad.

examples.trans: Are you not coming with us?

examples.text: Я прекрасно знаю, кто вы такой.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'could', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Сегодня не могу.
examples.trans: I can't today.

examples.text: Этого не может быть.
examples.trans: That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Не надо знать, надо просто подумать.
examples.trans: You do not need to know, you just need to think.

examples.text: Надо просто хорошо подумать.
examples.trans: You just need to think it over well.

examples.text: Может, он просто сидел в темноте?
examples.trans: Maybe he was just sitting in the dark?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask (a favour)', paired with 'просить'.

examples.text: Вы могли просто попросить меня остаться.
examples.trans: You could have simply asked me to stay.

examples.text: Я хотел тебя попросить.
examples.trans: I wanted to ask you something.

examples.text: Попроси маму.
examples.trans: Ask Mum.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: Вы могли просто попросить меня остаться.
examples.trans: You could have simply asked me to stay.

examples.text: Ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: There's nothing left.

examples.text: Я останусь дома.
examples.trans: I'll stay at home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты скажешь Свете, а я Никите.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вообще-то я его немного сам доработал.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will'.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Fine, I will write the resignation letter right now!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'зражать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to object, mind'.

examples.text: Гуля, ты не будешь сейчас возражать?
examples.trans: Gulya, will you not object right now?

examples.text: Ты же не возражаешь, Таня?
examples.trans: You do not mind, Tanya?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: If you cook worse, you will work for free!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.en: to do some work, to work for a bit
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'работать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to work for a while', paired with 'работать'.

examples.text: Если я ещё поработаю здесь су-шефом?
examples.trans: If I work here as sous-chef a bit longer?

examples.text: Надо немного поработать.
examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Я поработаю дома.
examples.trans: I'll do some work at home.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'у-шеф'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sous-chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Честно говоря, сегодня оно от су-шефа.
examples.trans: Honestly speaking, today it is from the sous-chef.

examples.text: Я хотел поговорить о нашем су-шефе.
examples.trans: I wanted to talk about our sous-chef.

examples.text: Он всегда был отличным надёжным су-шефом.
examples.trans: He has always been an excellent, reliable sous-chef.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sweet').

examples.text: Может, он дома просто электричество экономил?
examples.trans: Maybe he was just saving electricity at home?

examples.trans: Easy, darling, let me look at your eye right now.

examples.text: Скажи, правда же, мой милый Денис?
examples.trans: Tell them, is that not true, my darling Denis?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'держать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will support', paired with 'поддерживать'.

examples.text: Если поддержите меня, мы прорвёмся.
examples.trans: If you support me, we will break through.

examples.text: Друзья решили поддержать Самсона.
examples.trans: The friends decided to support Samson.

examples.text: Короче, мужики! Если поддержите меня, мы прорвёмся.
examples.trans: In short, guys! If you support me, we will break through.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('any').

examples.text: Я любое ваше блюдо легко приготовлю!
examples.trans: I will easily cook any dish of yours!

examples.text: А у нас всегда кипит любовь!
examples.trans: And love is always bubbling between us!

examples.text: Самое главное в жизни найти любовь.
examples.trans: The most important thing in life is to find love.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Может, он дома просто электричество экономил?
examples.trans: Maybe he was just saving electricity at home?

examples.text: Почему твоё заявление с маленькой буквы?

examples.text: Видишь, всё-таки твоему отцу очень одиноко.
examples.trans: You see, your father is very lonely after all.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'decision, ruling, solution' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я только за такое хорошее решение.
examples.trans: I am all for such a good decision.

examples.text: Решено, мы будем заказывать молекулярную кухню!
examples.trans: It is decided, we will order the molecular cuisine!

examples.text: Милый, я поддержу любое твоё решение.
examples.trans: Darling, I will support any decision of yours.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никита, у тебя сейчас есть минутка?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Then we will tell everything tomorrow.

examples.text: Тогда и будешь свои блюда дорабатывать!
examples.trans: Then you can modify your own dishes!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.text: А вы не пойдёте с нами?
examples.trans: Are you not coming with us?

examples.text: Ну, в принципе, можно и пойти.

examples.trans: So I cook poorly in the kitchen?

examples.text: Пиши заявление и уходи с кухни!
examples.trans: Write your resignation letter and leave the kitchen!

examples.text: Что такое новое блюдо молекулярной кухни?
examples.trans: What is this new molecular cuisine dish?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спокойной тебе ночи и сладких снов.
examples.trans: Good night to you and sweet dreams.

examples.text: Сейчас всё выглядит очень некрасиво.
examples.trans: Right now everything looks very bad.

examples.text: Поэтому мы должны всё честно рассказать.
examples.trans: Therefore we must tell everything honestly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Поэтому мы должны всё честно рассказать.
examples.trans: Therefore we must tell everything honestly.

examples.text: Я только за такое хорошее решение.
examples.trans: I am all for such a good decision.

examples.text: Катя, а ты уже совсем готова?
examples.trans: Katya, are you completely ready already?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Поэтому мы должны всё честно рассказать.
examples.trans: Therefore we must tell everything honestly.

examples.text: Денис, скорее, мы в кино опаздываем!
examples.trans: Denis, hurry, we are running late for the cinema!

examples.text: Пойдём, мы вас на улице подождём.
examples.trans: Let us go, we will wait for you outside.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'work' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хочу пригласить вас к себе на работу.
examples.trans: I want to invite you to work for me.

examples.text: Работать главным шеф-поваром, я не знаю.
examples.trans: To work as head chef, I do not know.

examples.text: А он позвал меня работать шефом.
examples.trans: And he invited me to work as a head chef.

meanings.en: to be late, to arrive late
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are late', paired with 'опоздать'.

examples.text: Денис, скорее, мы в кино опаздываем!
examples.trans: Denis, hurry, we are running late for the cinema!

examples.text: А то мы на работу опаздываем!
examples.trans: Otherwise we are running late for work!

examples.text: Народный кандидат не опаздывает!
examples.trans: The people's candidate isn't late!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'let us go', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я иду домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

examples.text: Он идёт на второй срок.
examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'it's time', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам пора наконец перестать так прятаться.
examples.trans: It is time for us to finally stop hiding like this.

examples.text: Жалко, кто теперь будет следить за порядком?
examples.trans: What a pity, who will keep order now?

examples.text: Ладно, мне пора, а вы отдыхайте.
examples.trans: Alright, I have to go, and you two relax.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Я вчера приготовил гостю ваше блюдо.
examples.trans: Yesterday I cooked your dish for a guest.

examples.text: Одно блюдо приготовил и уже шеф?
examples.trans: You cooked one dish and you are already a chef?

examples.text: Хорошо, договорились, сейчас готовим оба вслепую!
examples.trans: Fine, deal, right now we both cook blindfolded!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner, supper (evening meal)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Не надо лезть в чужие дела.
examples.trans: Do not meddle in other people's business.

examples.text: Ничего я в чужие дела не лезу!
examples.trans: I do not meddle in other people's business at all!

examples.text: Идёмте, Виктор Петрович, пора готовить ужин.
examples.trans: Let us go, Viktor Petrovich, it is time to cook dinner.
